what: a loft from a 20x20 square to the same square turned 45 degrees, 30 mm higher: its four side faces are strongly twisted ruled patches, the case a two-triangle mesh gets visibly wrong
method: At height 30t the section is the polygon of (1-t)p_i + t q_i (p_i the square's corners at angles 45+90k deg, q_i those at 90+90k deg, both radius 10 sqrt 2). Its shoelace area is quadratic in t, so Simpson is exact: A0=A1=400, A(1/2)= 2 r^2 (1 - ... ) computed from the midpoint polygon (a square of circumradius r cos(22.5 deg): area 2 r^2 cos^2(22.5 deg) = 400 cos^2(22.5 deg)=341.42). V = 30/6 (400 + 4*341.4214 + 400) = 5*(2165.6854)=10828.427. Faces: 4 sides and 2 caps.
